title: Build the first psychiatry medication identity allowlist
proposedRouting: Use the exact RxNorm Current Prescribable Content release for identity only, then curate a board-relevant psychiatry ingredient allowlist before any formulation, class, indication, safety, fit, formulary, case, or point behavior is added.
guidance: The user selected a psychiatry-first rather than all-U.S.-products approach. Start with common antidepressants, mood stabilizers, antipsychotics, anxiolytics, medications for common adverse effects, sleep, ADHD, and substance-use treatment. The current gap audit suggests an initial identity review that includes paroxetine, fluvoxamine, venlafaxine, desvenlafaxine, duloxetine, trazodone, lamotrigine, carbamazepine, risperidone, paliperidone, clozapine, ziprasidone, lurasidone, cariprazine, lorazepam, clonazepam, diazepam, hydroxyzine, prazosin, and benztropine. This is a proposed review list, not a recommendation, formulary, or authorization to bulk import. Resolve ingredient-versus-product granularity one decision at a time and keep aliases/RxCUIs out of the free-text class field.
resurfacingTrigger: Before implementing an RxNorm importer or adding more runtime medication definitions.

title: Audit the current medication tags and fit rules
proposedRouting: Inventory each current class/tag, author override, and active fit modifier; connect exact claims to formal contributions or preserve them as concise Developer opinion, then review clinical direction separately from game-point magnitude.
guidance: The current thirteen compatibility files are sufficient for the prototype but are not a sourced template for scale. Free-text class and mechanism/safety tags, plus active bupropion and mirtazapine fit concepts, need claim-level provenance. RxNorm can normalize identity but cannot support first-line status, contraindications, interactions, monitoring, comparative fit, or point values. Create smaller source requests by exact claim when the existing evidence catalog does not answer it.
resurfacingTrigger: When a medication tag or modifier is promoted, changed, or used to generate additional patients.

title: Separate therapy identity, fidelity, and gameplay availability
proposedRouting: Create one neutral file per reusable intervention and distinguish a generic family, referral, protocol-based therapy, informed-skills intervention, and full program before expanding the runtime menu.
guidance: Migrate CBT, behavioral activation, IPT, and supportive psychotherapy to the planned identity layer without changing current behavior. Treat DBT-informed skills separately from a complete DBT program. Keep CBT-I, ERP, CPT, prolonged exposure, motivational interviewing, and contingency management as unscored authoring candidates until their condition mappings, delivery capabilities, evidence contributions, combination/redundancy rules, and point balance are independently reviewed. Do not copy manuals, worksheets, or scripts.
resurfacingTrigger: Before adding new therapy choices or treating a menu label as delivery of a full program.

title: Stage common outpatient diagnosis identities without inventing criteria
proposedRouting: Add neutral identities only after deciding family granularity, then create separate tickets for criteria, focused actions, compatibility, treatment mappings, and balance.
guidance: The existing requested case families already have stable definitions. The clearest next identity gaps are panic disorder, social anxiety disorder, obsessive-compulsive disorder, ADHD, insomnia disorder, and adjustment disorder. Alcohol- and opioid-use disorders need a separate family-granularity decision because their treatment pathways differ. ICD-10-CM can support authoring search and NIMH can supply broad public-domain context, but neither silently supplies executable diagnostic criteria or treatment rules. Cyclothymia remains under its dedicated duration/source ticket.
resurfacingTrigger: Before adding a case from one of these families or exposing its treatment options.

title: Model medication regimen benefit, risk, and duplication
proposedRouting: Add normalized medication class, indication or role, and regimen-contributor records before a reusable combination evaluator. Compile each benefit, additive risk, interaction, duplication warning, and future exception into a separate trace item; never derive class membership by parsing the current free-text class labels.
guidance: Multiple new medications for the same indication should generally subtract from plan quality; same or overlapping class should create a strong duplicate warning. Benefits for distinct indications or evidence-supported augmentation may outweigh additive regimen risk, so the evaluator must not collapse all multi-medication plans into one penalty. Cross-titration is a future explicit exception and should remain disabled until its medication and timing state is modeled. Preserve clinical direction separately from provisional video-game point balance.
reviewerNotes: Developer opinion: Multiple new medications for one indication are generally a subtractor, and same- or overlapping-class starts warrant a strong duplicate warning. Distinct-indication or augmentation benefits can outweigh additive risk. Cross-titration should later be an explicit exception. Keep every contributor separately traceable; point weights remain provisional game balance.
resurfacingTrigger: Before implementing reusable medication-combination scoring, normalized class or indication relationships, or cross-titration.
